issues.title: Inverted renderer type check prevents circuit restart
issues.description: The condition checking for different renderer types has been inverted from `!==` to `===`. This causes the function to throw an error when the SAME renderer type tries to re-enable JS root components (e.g., during circuit restart), which is the exact scenario that should be allowed. The original intent was to throw an error only when a DIFFERENT renderer type attempts to enable root components. This bug breaks circuit restart functionality, causing applications to fail when users reconnect after a circuit disconnect.

issues.title: Missing parameter update causes stale data on circuit restart
issues.description: The assignment `jsComponentParametersByIdentifier = jsComponentParameters;` has been removed from the re-enabling logic. When a circuit restarts and `enableJSRootComponents` is called again with new parameters, the global `jsComponentParametersByIdentifier` is not updated. This causes the application to continue using stale parameters from the previous circuit. The `DynamicRootComponent` class constructor and methods rely on `jsComponentParametersByIdentifier` to retrieve component parameter definitions, so they will operate with outdated metadata after a circuit restart.

issues.title: Test method missing Arrange/Act/Assert comments
issues.description: The added test method does not contain explicit '// Arrange', '// Act', and '// Assert' (or '// Act & Assert') comments to delineate the AAA phases, violating the required test structure convention.
issues.rule_name: Test Methods Must Use Arrange-Act-Assert Pattern with Comments

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #64536 - Allow JS root components to reinitialize on circuit restart

structured_output.summary:
The PR is meant to let `enableJSRootComponents` be called again when the same renderer type starts a new circuit. It adds a `rendererId` parameter, tracks `currentRendererId`, and uses a `hasInitializedJsComponents` flag so the JS initializers only run once. It also undoes an earlier test refactor: the separate test file and extra TestServer host are deleted, the dynamic-JS-root test moves into `StatePersistenceTest`, and `RazorComponentEndpointsStartup` now always registers `dynamic-js-root-counter`.

There are two bugs in the core function, and together they break the feature. First, the guard is reversed. It throws when `currentRendererId === rendererId`, which is exactly the circuit restart the PR wants to allow. A different renderer type gets through, which is the multi-host case it should reject. The comment directly under the condition describes the opposite of what the code does. Second, the refactor removed `jsComponentParametersByIdentifier = jsComponentParameters`, so that module variable is never set. Every `Blazor.rootComponents.add()` call will throw a `TypeError` once `AddRootComponent` returns, even on the very first circuit. Because of that, the test this PR moves in (`PersistentStateIsSupportedInDynamicJSRoots`) should fail too. No test covers the actual circuit-restart scenario.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The renderer-ID check is reversed, so the scenario the PR exists to fix still throws and the multi-host case it should reject is allowed. A dropped assignment also breaks `Blazor.rootComponents.add()` for every caller. Both are core regressions.

architecture.overview:
When a Blazor renderer (Server circuit, WebAssembly, or WebView) attaches its interop methods, `attachWebRendererInterop` in `WebRendererInteropMethods.ts` checks whether any JS-registered root components came with it. If so, it calls `enableJSRootComponents` in `JSRootComponents.ts`. That function stores the renderer's .NET manager object and the parameter metadata for each component identifier in module-level variables, then runs any JS initializers (for example, custom-element registration). Later, `Blazor.rootComponents.add()` reads those variables to call `AddRootComponent` on .NET and to build a `DynamicRootComponent`.

This PR passes `rendererId` into `enableJSRootComponents` and tracks it in `currentRendererId`. The goal is that a re-enable from the same renderer type (a new circuit) swaps in the new manager, while a different renderer type throws. A `hasInitializedJsComponents` flag stops the initializers from running twice. On the test side, the dedicated `StatePersistanceJSRootTest` file and the extra TestServer host are removed, and `RazorComponentEndpointsStartup` now always registers `dynamic-js-root-counter`.
steps: Start at `CircuitManager.ts` and the WebAssembly/WebView startup code. Each calls `attachWebRendererInterop(rendererId, interopMethods, jsComponentParameters, jsComponentInitializers)` when its renderer becomes ready.
`WebRendererInteropMethods.ts`: if JS component parameters are present, it now forwards `rendererId` to `enableJSRootComponents`.

`JSRootComponents.ts` `enableJSRootComponents`: compares `rendererId` with `currentRendererId` to decide whether to throw or replace the stored `manager`, then runs initializers once, gated by `hasInitializedJsComponents`.
`RootComponentsFunctions.add()`: uses `getRequiredManager()` plus `jsComponentParametersByIdentifier` to create a `DynamicRootComponent` and push its initial parameters.

Tests: `RazorComponentEndpointsStartup` always calls `RegisterForJavaScript` for `dynamic-js-root-counter`, and `StatePersistenceTest.PersistentStateIsSupportedInDynamicJSRoots` exercises it through `dynamic-js-root.html`.

findings.title: Renderer-ID guard is reversed: circuit restart throws, multi-host is allowed
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/Web.JS/src/Rendering/JSRootComponents.ts`, `enableJSRootComponents` (around lines 126-130) throws when `currentRendererId === rendererId`. That is backwards: a re-enable from the same renderer type (circuit restart) should be accepted, and a different renderer type (multi-host) should throw. Change the comparison to `currentRendererId !== rendererId` so the code matches the comments in the function and the PR description. If possible, add an E2E test that restarts a Server circuit on a page using `Blazor.rootComponents.add()` and checks that the component can still be added afterwards.

findings.title: `jsComponentParametersByIdentifier` is never assigned, so `rootComponents.add()` throws a TypeError
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/Web.JS/src/Rendering/JSRootComponents.ts`, `enableJSRootComponents` no longer assigns the module-level `jsComponentParametersByIdentifier`. The assignment was lost when the initializer loop was refactored around lines 136-150. Because of this, `RootComponentsFunctions.add()` (line 30) throws a TypeError when it indexes into undefined. Add `jsComponentParametersByIdentifier = jsComponentParameters;` right after `manager = managerInstance;`, outside the `hasInitializedJsComponents` guard, so it is refreshed on every enable.

findings.title: No test covers the circuit-restart scenario this PR fixes
findings.fixPrompt: Add an E2E test for dotnet/aspnetcore#64523: on a page that uses `Blazor.rootComponents.add()` with a Server render mode, force the circuit to end and a new one to start (for example pause/resume, or disconnect with `DisconnectedCircuitMaxRetained = 0` followed by a restart). Assert that no 'Dynamic root components have already been enabled' error appears and that a dynamic root component can be added and works after the restart. Put it next to `PersistentStateIsSupportedInDynamicJSRoots` in `src/Components/test/E2ETest/Tests/StatePersistenceTest.cs`, or in a related circuit test file.

findings.title: Unconditional `RegisterForJavaScript` changes behavior for every test using `RazorComponentEndpointsStartup`
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/test/testassets/Components.TestServer/RazorComponentEndpointsStartup.cs` line 54, `RegisterForJavaScript<ComponentWithPersistentState>("dynamic-js-root-counter")` now runs for every app using this startup. Confirm this is intentional. If it is, run the full Components E2E suite, especially the circuit pause/resume and reconnection tests, after fixing the `enableJSRootComponents` guard, to check that turning on JS root components everywhere causes no regressions. If it is not, restore the configuration-gated registration.

findings.title: Running JS initializers only once is the right call
findings.body: The `hasInitializedJsComponents` flag is a good addition. Initializers often call things like `customElements.define`, which throws if the same name is registered twice, so running them again on a circuit restart would be harmful. The decision not to dispose the stale manager is also well reasoned in the comments: its circuit is gone, so disposing it would raise `JSDisconnectedException`. Once the guard and the missing assignment are fixed, this design holds up.
